statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-86597 is an insertion of sensitive information into log files in the Snowflake JDBC driver before 4.3.4. Liquibase Secure 6.0.0 bundles snowflake-jdbc 4.3.3. When a user routes driver logs into the Liquibase log with --log-channels=all (or net.snowflake) and --log-level=FINE or lower, the driver writes the query-result encryption key (qrmk) in clear text to the Liquibase log file. Liquibase log redaction does not apply to third-party log records. The qrmk is generated by Snowflake for a single query and only decrypts that query's result chunks in Snowflake-managed cloud storage. It is not a credential and does not grant access to the Snowflake account. The pre-signed URLs needed to download those chunks are logged with their signature masked, so the key alone does not expose query results; an attacker would also need the full URL from another source while it remains valid (6 hours). The default log configuration (liquibase channel only) does not expose this data.
statements.action_statement: Upgrade to the next Liquibase Secure release, which bundles snowflake-jdbc 4.3.4. Until then, do not enable driver debug logging (--log-channels=all or --log-channels=net.snowflake at FINE or lower, or the driver's own tracing / sf_client_config.json) against Snowflake, and delete existing Liquibase log files produced with those settings.
